The existing applyLockedSchema rail already gives one advisory-locked client with 42501 savepoint tolerance, and key 47110008 is unused. What's left: add the key, pass it, rewrite the catch so it re-probes and branches (present, absent, can't verify), and add a spec that forces the DDL to fail and checks the level and wording for each branch.

entries.title: Trading DB specs race on schema bootstrap
entries.why: The trading schema bootstrap still runs without a lock. No trading module passes a lockKey, so two concurrent bootstraps can interleave the DROP TRIGGER / CREATE TRIGGER pair. The fix is small: add SCHEMA_LOCK_KEYS entries for trading and books and pass them. Proving it means running the DB-backed trading specs in parallel against a throwaway Postgres, since unpointed runs are refused.
entries.evidence: src/app/trading-schema.ts:42-45: bootstrapTradingSchema calls ensureBooksSchema, then runRuntimeSchemaBootstrap with no lockKey. `git grep lockKey -- src/app/trading*.ts` finds nothing, so src/shared/services/database/schema-bootstrap-policy.ts:143-147 takes the unlocked per-statement path. src/app/trading-schema.ts:137-138 has the DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_trd_signals_book_fill / CREATE TRIGGER pair that collides. The three specs named in the entry exist: tests/unit/trading-books-schema.spec.ts, trading-event-plans.spec.ts and trading-pinned-lots.spec.ts. tests/helpers/spec-database-url.ts:52-63 throws on an unpointed run, so the green run needs a disposable database.

(4) The residue survey needs rows deleted from the live trading database. That last part needs the operator's authorisation, because one book row still has orders, which is why it fell outside the earlier authorised delete.

No DSN is set, so tests/helpers/spec-database-url.ts:52-63 throws for every spec that resolves through it. tests/unit/trading-watchdog-books.spec.ts:29: `const DB_CONTAINER = process.env.OSHAL_TEST_DB_CONTAINER || 'oshal-local-db';`. entries.title: Scheduled Local CI unattended proof
entries.why: The unattended 23:30 run on 2026-09-14 meets all three clauses. Its log names archive-ref=origin/main and pins the SHA that origin/main pointed at when the run started. Task Scheduler's last result (1) equals the failed gate's exit code (1). The launcher now propagates that exit code (VBS entry 3, ci-local.sh entry 17), and tests/unit/ci-local-scheduled-ref.spec.ts guards it.
entries.evidence: %LOCALAPPDATA%\oshal\ci-local.log line 3125: `[2026-09-14T23:30:04] === LOCAL CI start (scheduled=1 head=1 ...) node-source=origin/main archive-ref=origin/main sha=018e0a74cf09 posture=scheduled-origin-main ===`, ending `=== LOCAL CI: FAILED gates: typecheck unit security-policy local-secret-hygiene e2e-green trivy ===`. Reflog `refs/remotes/origin/main@{2026-09-14 23:27:48}` = 018e0a74. The next main commit, 09503c5d, was authored 23:30:20, after the run started, and `git log 018e0a74..09503c5d` holds only that commit, so the run judged the real remote tip. Get-ScheduledTaskInfo 'OSHAL Local CI': LastRunTime 9/14/2026 11:30:01 PM, LastTaskResult 1, trigger daily 23:30. scripts/ci-local.sh:648 `exit 1` on failed gates. scripts/ci-local-hidden.vbs: `exitCode = sh.Run(command, 0, True)` / `WScript.Quit exitCode`. Earlier scheduled runs (08-30 to 09-12) log the same archive-ref=origin/main shape. This proof lives only in local logs, so closing should record a dated note.
verifyReasons:
CONFIRMED: I checked each clause myself and could not refute any of them. The 2026-09-14 23:30 run meets all three.

1. **The log names `archive-ref=origin/main`.** Line 3125 of `%LOCALAPPDATA%\oshal\ci-local.log` and line 1 of `ci-local-last-run.log` both read `scheduled=1 head=1 ... node-source=origin/main archive-ref=origin/main sha=018e0a74cf09 posture=scheduled-origin-main`. That posture is only set when the scheduled fetch succeeds and the fetched ref can be read (`resolve_source_commit` in `scripts/ci-local.sh`).

2. **It records the exact fetched SHA.**
   - The start line records a 12-character short SHA, which `git rev-parse` resolves to 018e0a74cf093f98194e34af7121900ed58ccadf.
   - The full run log also prints the full 40-character SHA at line 38 (`Pinned core=018e0a74cf09...`), which comes from the same pinned `$SOURCE_SHA`.
   - The reflog shows origin/main at 018e0a74 from 23:27:48 until 23:30:25. The fetch at 23:30:01-04 left no reflog entry, so the ref did not move.
   - The next commit, 09503c5d, was committed at 23:30:20, after the fetch. Its parent is 018e0a74, and it is the only commit in `018e0a74..09503c5d`. So the run judged the real remote tip.

3. **Task Scheduler's result equals the exit code of the completed run.**
   - I ran `Get-ScheduledTaskInfo` myself. It shows LastRunTime 9/14/2026 11:30:01 PM, LastTaskResult 1 and State Ready, and the task is not still running.
   - It is the only scheduled task that launches ci-local. Its action is `wscript.exe //B //Nologo C:\Projects\oshal\scripts\ci-local-hidden.vbs`.
   - That launcher runs `sh.Run(command, 0, True)` and then `WScript.Quit exitCode`, so it waits and passes the code through. This has been committed since 76d5788e (#142). The old launcher did not wait, so it could only ever report 0.
   - The run log ends with the FAILED-gates line, the alert headline and `SEND_OK`. In the version that ran (018e0a74, line 620) the next statement is `exit 1`, and the EXIT trap does not change that status.

**The run was unprompted.** It started at the trigger time, and only one start line appears, at 23:30:04. According to COLLABORATE.md, the only agent action on the task that day was re-enabling it at about 06:04Z, after it had been disabled for the 09-13 run. Re-enabling is not a launch. StartBoundary is still 2026-07-14, so the task was not re-created either.

**Two small errors in the triage evidence, neither of which weakens the 09-14 proof:**
- `ci-local.sh:648` points at the current file. The version that actually ran has `exit 1` at line 620. The diff between them only adds the spec-database-default and alert-residue gates; it does not touch how the source commit is chosen or how the script exits.
- The claim that every scheduled run from 08-30 to 09-12 used origin/main is wrong for 09-09. That run fell back to local HEAD after a failed fetch (`DEGRADED_FETCH_FAILED_HEAD_FALLBACK`, `archive-ref=HEAD`).

**The evidence is local and short-lived.** The full run log and LastTaskResult will both be overwritten by the next 23:30 run. Task Scheduler history is disabled, so there is no event log to fall back on. Closing the entry should therefore record a dated note of this proof.

CONFIRMED: I couldn't refute it. I checked each of the three done-when clauses myself against the unprompted 2026-09-14 23:30 run, and all three hold.

(1) **The log names `archive-ref=origin/main`.** `%LOCALAPPDATA%\oshal\ci-local.log` line 3125 reads `[2026-09-14T23:30:04] ... scheduled=1 ... archive-ref=origin/main sha=018e0a74cf09 posture=scheduled-origin-main`. The run finished at 01:12:43 with `FAILED gates: typecheck unit security-policy local-secret-hygiene e2e-green trivy`.

(2) **It records the exact fetched SHA, and that SHA was the real remote tip.**
- The summary log carries the 12-char short SHA. That is by design: `SOURCE_SHORT_SHA` at `scripts/ci-local.sh` line 205, and the original fix spec asked for a short SHA.
- The full run log `ci-local-last-run.log` line 38 carries the full value: `Pinned core=018e0a74cf093f98194e34af7121900ed58ccadf`.
- The reflog `git log -g refs/remotes/origin/main` shows origin/main set to 018e0a74 at 23:27:48, then 09503c5d at 23:30:25 from another agent's `fetch -q origin main`.
- There is no reflog entry for the CI's own fetch (`git fetch --quiet origin +refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main`), so that fetch at about 23:30:04 updated nothing: the remote was still at 018e0a74.
- 09503c5d was committed at 23:30:20 and its parent is 018e0a74, so no newer commit existed at fetch time.
- A failed fetch would have logged a `DEGRADED_*` posture instead of `scheduled-origin-main`.

(3) **Task Scheduler's result equals the run's exit code.**
- `Get-ScheduledTaskInfo 'OSHAL Local CI'` returns LastRunTime 9/14/2026 11:30:01 PM, LastTaskResult 1, NumberOfMissedRuns 0.
- The task definition in `C:\Windows\System32\Tasks\OSHAL Local CI` has a daily 23:30 trigger. Its action is `wscript.exe //B //Nologo C:\Projects\oshal\scripts\ci-local-hidden.vbs`, which is this trunk. No ExecutionTimeLimit is set, so the 1h42m run was not killed.
- The run log ends with the failure headline and then `SEND_OK`. The only path after that in `ci-local.sh` is `exit 1` (line 648), and the EXIT trap `on_exit` does not change the exit status.
- The launcher `scripts/ci-local-hidden.vbs` uses `sh.Run(command, 0, True)` and `WScript.Quit exitCode`. It has been unchanged since 76d5788e (2026-08-06) and is clean in the working tree.
- `tests/unit/ci-local-scheduled-ref.spec.ts` runs the launcher against an exit-37 stub, so the result of 1 is a propagated code, not a generic 1.

**The script did not change during the run.** The version that ran was 3754a367 (20:55 on 09-14). The later edits, fcd68539 and a4f6d4d4, landed at 01:23 and 01:40, after the run ended at 01:12.

**Caveats.** The proof lives only in local logs outside the tree. The full-SHA copy in `ci-local-last-run.log` will be overwritten by tonight's 23:30 run, so closing the entry should include a dated note quoting these lines.

entries.title: CI Playwright red-baseline retirement
entries.why: Most Playwright specs are still outside the green ratchet. 11 specs still hardcode an origin. There is no disposition list for unsupported cases. The ratchet itself is red, and the gate still runs with --retries=2. This is a multi-part normalisation of the e2e corpus, and proving it needs the Docker Postgres and Redis datastores.

entries.why: No fix exists yet. The runner still bind-mounts a mode-0700 mkdtemp dir at /work with no uid mapping, chmod or --user handling. entries.title: CI secret-scanner remote mutation proof
entries.why: A remote proof needs a hosted GitHub Actions run of the gitleaks job. Every workflow that runs it is manual-dispatch-only because hosted-runner minutes are the account's binding constraint. The proof also means pushing a secret-shaped fixture to this public repo. The fail-closed pre-push publish gate exists to refuse that push, and it must not be bypassed. The history scan uses `--log-opts=--all`, so the planted commit would stay scannable, and fetchable by SHA, after the fact. Only the operator can authorise the spend and the push, or re-scope the proof to the local ci-local secret-scan gate.
entries.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:41-42 and .github/workflows/security.yml:23-24 are both `on: workflow_dispatch` only ('MANUAL ONLY', operator decision 2026-08-06). security.yml:158-181 runs gitleaks `detect --log-opts="--all"` over full history plus a `--no-git` worktree pass. publish-gate.yml runs scripts/publish-gate.sh on pull_request, and that gate scans vendor-prefixed credentials (publish-gate.sh changelog entry 1). The archived history (docs/backlog/archive/2026-08-05-partial-item-history.md:783-787) records run 29048082693 green, with 'a real planted test secret makes secret-scan red (still open)'.
entries.operatorAsk: Do you approve (a) one paid workflow_dispatch run of the Security or CI secret-scan job on a disposable branch, and (b) pushing a synthetic secret-shaped fixture to the public oshal repo past the pre-push publish gate, with the branch deleted afterwards? Or do you re-scope the done-when to a planted-fixture fail-then-pass of the local `ci-local.sh` secret-scan gate?
entries.decision: RE-SCOPED to the local ci-local.sh secret-scan gate (planted fixture red->green in a throwaway export, never pushed); LOW priority - only when the box has headroom (operator, 2026-09-20)

entries.title: Surface-bridge ops have no success-path log line
entries.why: An emitted-ops turn now logs op count, op names and the target app at INFO, next to the custom-op names the surface declared, so the BUG-18 mismatch shows up in the api log alone. A regression test covers it. The BACKLOG text still reads 'Remaining' only because a later commit removed the Done text that #466 wrote.
entries.evidence: src/app/routes/jarvis-routes.ts:875-884 calls `logger.info({ sessionId, app, screen, ops: surfaceOps.length, opNames: surfaceOps.map(describeSurfaceOp), declaredCustomOps }, 'jarvis: surface ops returned to the surface')`. describeSurfaceOp at :203-205 renders a custom op as `custom:<name>`. This landed in df652727 (#466). The guard is tests/unit/jarvis-surface-context.spec.ts:284-360 ('/ask — an emitted-ops turn is diagnosable from the api log alone'): it asserts exactly one INFO line with opNames ['custom:update_master_resume_summary'] and declaredCustomOps ['resume_action'], which is the BUG-18 shape. `git log -S'surface ops returned to the surface' -- docs/BACKLOG.md` shows df652727 adding the Done text and fea4f721 (#471) removing it.
verifyReasons:
CONFIRMED: I tried to refute the claim and couldn't. I checked both done-when criteria myself against the current tree (HEAD b999b05f), and both are met.

**Criterion 1: an emitted-ops turn logs op count, names and the target app at INFO.**
- `src/app/routes/jarvis-routes.ts:875-884` is in the /ask success path, right after `extractSurfaceDirectives` and the artifact check. When `surfaceOps.length && surfaceContext`, it calls `logger.info({ sessionId, app: surfaceContext.app, screen: surfaceContext.surface, ops: surfaceOps.length, opNames: surfaceOps.map(describeSurfaceOp), declaredCustomOps: (surfaceContext.customOps ?? []).map(op => op.name) }, 'jarvis: surface ops returned to the surface')`.
- `describeSurfaceOp` (:203-205) renders a custom op as `custom:<name>` and any other op as its name.
- The logger (:176) is a plain pino child (`src/shared/logger/logger.ts`). Its level defaults to 'info'. The api service in `docker-compose.oshal-local.yml` gets `LOG_LEVEL: info` from the `*bot-env` anchor, and that value is fixed in the file rather than an env override. None of the logged fields appear in `LOG_REDACT_OPTIONS`.
- The routes are mounted in the api process (`src/app/server.ts:1413`), so the line lands in the api log.
- No commit has touched `jarvis-routes.ts`, `jarvis-directives.ts`, `jarvis-surface-context.ts` or the spec since df652727.

**Criterion 2: the BUG-18 shape is diagnosable from the api log alone.**
- BUG-18 (`docs/operations/bug-log.md:894`) was a well-formed `custom` op named `update_master_resume_summary` on the Jarvis /ask path, where Resume Studio handles `resume_action`.
- The surface publishes the custom names it handles in `ContextSchema.customOps`. `jarvis.html:1488` forwards that snapshot unchanged, and `normalizeAskSurfaceContext` keeps it.
- So the log line puts the emitted `custom:<name>` next to the declared names, and a mismatch shows up in one grep of the api log. If a surface declares no names, `declaredCustomOps` is an empty list, which still shows the mismatch.

**The regression test.** `tests/unit/jarvis-surface-context.spec.ts:284-360` is in the vitest include (`tests/unit/**/*.spec.ts`) and has no skip markers.
- It drives the real router and the real `extractSurfaceDirectives`. Only the model, credential brokers, database bootstrap and logger are doubled.
- It asserts exactly one INFO line with `opNames ['custom:update_master_resume_summary']` and `declaredCustomOps ['resume_action']`.
- A second case asserts that a turn with no screen context logs only the existing WARN.
- I did not run it, because this check was read-only.

**Why the entry still reads "Remaining".**
- `git log -S'surface ops returned to the surface' -- docs/BACKLOG.md` shows df652727 (#466) adding the Done text and fea4f721 (#471) removing it.
- #471 is a trading-assessment docs commit whose message never mentions Jarvis. Its diff puts the original "Remaining" text back, so it reads as a stale-tree overwrite, not a deliberate reopening.

**What I ruled out.**
- Two paths drop ops silently: an artifact-scoped turn (`artifactSelection` or `artifactReply.hadDirective`), and ops that fail validation. In both, the ops never reach a surface. The entry is about delivered ops that a surface then ignores, so these paths are outside its scope.
- The client-side `relayReply` path in swarmbot-chat and workflow-studio is not the jarvis-routes path the entry names.

REFUTED: The code half holds up. At HEAD b999b05f, src/app/routes/jarvis-routes.ts:875-884 writes an INFO line on the success path with app, screen, op count, opNames (custom:<name>, from describeSurfaceOp at :203-205) and declaredCustomOps. No commit after df652727 touches jarvis-routes.ts, jarvis-surface-context.ts, jarvis-directives.ts, the surface-bridge types or jarvis.html. The client forwards the context verbatim, including customOps (src/api/jarvis.html:570-571, :1488). The api logs at INFO (docker-compose.oshal-local.yml x-bot-env LOG_LEVEL: info, which oshal-api merges and does not override). None of the logged fields are on the logger's redaction list. I also confirmed df652727 (#466) wrote the Done text and fea4f721 (#471) put back a stale copy.

The evidence still does not prove the claim in the current tree:

(1) The guard cited for this entry cannot pass at HEAD. tests/unit/jarvis-surface-context.spec.ts:27-30 replaces @/shared/services/database with a factory that exports only createOptionalPostgresPool, ensureConversationStoreSchema, runRuntimeSchemaBootstrap and buildOwnerRlsPolicyStatements. The HEAD commit b999b05f changed both store constructors (src/entities/task/services/in-memory-task-store.ts:64 and src/entities/message/services/in-memory-message-store.ts:53) to call createPersistenceActivation from that same barrel. It did not update this spec: `git log df652727..HEAD -- tests/unit/jarvis-surface-context.spec.ts` is empty. The only spec that references createPersistenceActivation is persistence-mode-readiness.spec.ts. The '/ask — an emitted-ops turn is diagnosable from the api log alone' block builds `new InMemoryTaskStore()` and `new InMemoryMessageStore()` in its beforeEach (:302-303). With vitest ^4.1.9, reading an export the mock factory does not define throws. So both cases should fail before any log assertion runs. "A regression test covers it" is therefore false for the current tree. (I did not run the spec, since this review is read-only.)

(2) The second criterion is about the api log itself ("diagnosable from the api log alone"), and it was never shown there. The spec mocks @/shared/logger, so it records a call to a stand-in, not a line in the api's log output. df652727's own Done text said the running api would only carry the line "after the next core deploy". No api-log observation of an emitted-ops turn is recorded anywhere. docs/operations/bug-log.md (end of the BUG-18 entry) still lists the success-path log as "Related gap, not yet fixed."

The line looks correct in the code, but its only test is broken at HEAD and the api-log claim was never observed, so the entry should not be closed yet.

entries.title: The nightly can wedge for hours deleting its own previous export
entries.why: The done-when is met for the purge and is on origin/main. Both exports are purged through a timed, fail-loud helper. A purge FAIL fails head-src, and the run still continues to secret-scan, unpushed-commits and its outcome line. A spec covers the timeout and abandon paths. The entry's 'Remaining' item (the unbounded git archive | tar step, still unbounded at ci-local.sh:219) is outside this done-when by the entry's own words. Keep it as a new entry if wanted.
entries.evidence: Commit 3754a367 (#468), an ancestor of origin/main (git merge-base --is-ancestor OK), plus follow-up ea5d1ae0. scripts/ci-local.sh:217 `purge_tree "$GATE_SRC" || return 1` (prepare_head_src) and :399/:405 (gate_secrets). scripts/ci/ci-purge.sh has the watchdog (CI_PURGE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, one purge: OK|FAIL|REFUSED line). tests/unit/ci-local-purge.spec.ts covers the timeout, native-child abandon, REFUSED roots, and the `purge_tree ... || return 1` pins. On head-src failure, ci-local.sh sets NODE_GATES_OK=0 and still runs secret-scan, local-secret-hygiene and unpushed-commits and writes the FAILED outcome line. The real-export measurement (70s OK) is recorded in the #468 PR body.
verifyReasons:
REFUTED: The entry is not done. The code does what the triage agent says, but one of the three original done-when criteria has never been shown to hold.

The original done-when, from commit 7d0db10d (#423), has three parts: (1) both purges are timeout-bounded and fail loud; (2) the delete clears a real node_modules export on this box in minutes; (3) "a run that inherits a leftover export from a failed run reaches its gates and writes an outcome line."

Part 1 is met. `scripts/ci/ci-purge.sh` has a watchdog (default 600 s) and prints exactly one OK/FAIL/REFUSED line. `scripts/ci-local.sh:217` and `:399`/`:401`/`:405` call it with `|| return 1` / `|| rc=1`. The spec covers the timeout path.

Part 3 is claimed, never demonstrated:
- **No run has inherited a leftover since the fix.** In `%LOCALAPPDATA%\oshal\ci-local.log`, the only post-fix nightly (2026-09-14 23:30, sha 018e0a74cf09) logs `purge: OK .../ci-src (already absent)`. The manual 70 s measurement had already deleted the leftover. `ci-local-last-run.log` and `ci-runs/` hold no other ci-src purge line.
- **No test covers it either.** `tests/unit/ci-local-purge.spec.ts` runs `purge_tree` on its own and only checks by text search that the two gates call `purge_tree ... || return 1`. Nothing runs `ci-local.sh` or its gate sequence against a leftover export. The "continues to the outcome line" claim comes from reading the code.
- **A leftover now exists.** `ci-src` has been on disk since Sep 15 01:05, so tonight's run is the first real test.

The code reasoning also does not deliver part 3 in either case:
- **If the purge fails:** head-src fails, so `NODE_GATES_OK=0` and `SKIP_E2E=1` (`ci-local.sh:556-578`). Typecheck, unit, lint, connectors, manifests, kernel-skills, security-policy, repo-separation, spec-database-default, worktree-strays and e2e are all skipped. The run writes an outcome line but does not reach its gates. `GATE_SRC` was set to the old export at line 213, before the purge, and is never reset. So `gate_kernel_skills_image` (line 459) and `gate_trivy`'s `.trivyignore` read (line 524) then use the half-deleted tree from the previous commit.
- **If the purge succeeds:** reaching the gates depends on `git archive | tar` at line 219. The entry's own Remaining says that step is still unbounded.

Part 2 rests on one manual `purge_tree` call outside any `ci-local.sh` run: 70 s on 36,048 files, per the PR body and the lane's log. The only in-run measurement on this box is different. During the 2026-09-15 nightly, purging `ci-scan-src` (5,598 source files, no node_modules) took 97 s (`[2026-09-15T01:02:11] purge: OK .../ci-scan-src (97s)`). So the manual 70 s figure does not show how the purge performs inside a real run.

REFUTED: The claim is refuted: the third done-when criterion has never been shown to hold. Only the first criterion is clearly met.

What I confirmed:
- Commit 3754a367 (#468) is on origin/main (HEAD = origin/main = b999b05f).
- Criterion 1 (purge bounded and fails loud) is met. scripts/ci-local.sh:217 has `purge_tree "$GATE_SRC" || return 1`. gate_secrets calls it at :399, :401 and :405. The watchdog is at scripts/ci/ci-purge.sh:160-192 (default limit 600s, abandons the process tree, prints one OK/FAIL/REFUSED line). tests/unit/ci-local-purge.spec.ts covers the timeout and abandon paths.

What fails:

1. Criterion 3 is unproven. It reads: "a run that inherits a leftover export from a failed run reaches its gates and writes an outcome line." That is something a real run has to show, and no run has.
   - Only one scheduled run has used the new code (2026-09-14 23:30, sha 018e0a74). Line 3127 of %LOCALAPPDATA%\oshal\ci-local.log shows it inherited nothing: `purge: OK %LOCALAPPDATA%\oshal\ci-src (already absent)`. The manual 70s purge had already removed the leftover.
   - No test drives ci-local.sh through a run that inherits an export. The spec runs the helper on synthetic trees and checks the `|| return 1` text. It never runs a real nightly.
   - The "met" wording was written into the backlog by the lane that made the fix. For this criterion it rests on reading the code, not on an observed run.

2. The code-reading argument only covers part of the criterion.
   - On a purge FAIL, ci-local.sh:557 and :575-577 set NODE_GATES_OK=0. That skips typecheck, unit, lint, connectors, manifests, kernel-skills and e2e, so the run does not reach those gates.
   - ci-purge.sh:180 also leaves the tree in place ("remove it by hand before the next run"). Every later night inherits it again.
   - So "reaches its gates" holds only if the purge finishes inside 600s during a real run. That has never been seen for a node_modules export.

3. The "clears it in minutes" evidence (criterion 2) comes from a single measurement taken outside any run.
   - The 70s purge never appears in ci-local.log. The PR #468 body itself said no count survived on disk. A later commit, 216f6ecf, says a log survives, but I could not find it.
   - The only purge timed inside a run is ci-scan-src: 5,598 files, no node_modules, 97s (ci-local.log:3155). That is far slower per file than the manual measurement.

4. The first real test has not happened yet. The failed 2026-09-15 01:05 run left %LOCALAPPDATA%\oshal\ci-src behind, node_modules included. Tonight's 23:30 run will be the first to inherit an export under the new code. The entry stays open until a logged run shows the purge result and gets to its gates and the outcome line.

entries.title: `secret-scan` reports PASS even when gitleaks could not read part of the tree
entries.why: Met and merged. gate_secrets goes through run_secret_scan, which counts the scanner's skipped or unread stderr lines. It fails on any count above zero or any non-zero scanner exit code, and writes the unread=N of M count into the verdict line. A spec replays the image's real stderr through a stand-in docker and shows a partial scan does not pass.
entries.evidence: Commit 3754a367 (#468) on origin/main. scripts/ci-local.sh:404 `run_secret_scan "$exp" gitleaks_container_scan "$exp" || rc=1`. scripts/ci/ci-secret-scan.sh:16 GITLEAKS_UNREAD_PATTERN, and :37-52 return 1 when unread>0 or rc!=0, with the 'secret-scan: FAIL unread=N of M exported files' line. tests/unit/ci-local-secret-scan.spec.ts:136-160 (FAIL unread=2 of 3, FAIL unread=1 of 3 for the 2026-09-10 wording, PASS unread=0, FAIL scanner rc=1).
verifyReasons:
REFUTED: Most of the fix is real and merged, but the proof criterion is met only because the implementing commit rewrote it.

What is met:
- 3754a367 (#468) is an ancestor of HEAD, and the helper has not changed since.
- `gate_secrets` (scripts/ci-local.sh:397-407) calls `run_secret_scan "$exp" gitleaks_container_scan "$exp" || rc=1`.
- scripts/ci/ci-secret-scan.sh:34-52 fails when rc!=0 or unread>0.
- The count reaches the real log. `%LOCALAPPDATA%\oshal\ci-local.log` shows the 2026-09-15 nightly writing `secret-scan: PASS unread=0 of 5598 exported files (scanner rc=0)`, with the scanner's INF lines replayed into ci-local-last-run.log just before it. Criteria 1 and 3 hold for the wordings the pattern knows.

What is not met:
1. **The done-when was rewritten in the same commit as the fix.** #443 (9f482e89) required "a run with a deliberately unreadable file in the export is shown not to pass". 3754a367 changed that to "a deliberately unreadable path ... (the stand-in replays the real wording ...)" and marked it met.
2. **The spec has no unreadable file.** In tests/unit/ci-local-secret-scan.spec.ts the fixture export is 3 readable files (.gitleaks.toml, README.md, src/app.ts). A scripted stand-in `docker` prints skip lines for `/scan/config-seed/hidden.json` and `/scan/src/private`, which do not exist in that export. The real gitleaks image never runs against an unreadable path in any test, and no on-disk log shows one. So the spec proves the stderr-counting branch, not the stated outcome.
3. **The mocked boundary is the one that failed.** The defect is the scanner image's behaviour: exit 0, plus what it writes for unread paths. CLAUDE.md's integration-boundary rule says a mock-only test is not closure evidence for the mocked boundary, and that scoped doubles must be recorded with a real companion in docs/governance/real-boundary-regression-audit.md. That file has no gitleaks, secret-scan or ci-local-secret-scan entry.
4. **"Replays the image's real stderr" is only partly true.** The spec's "2026-09-10 wording" line (`ERR could not read file path=... error="read ...: cannot allocate memory"`) is rebuilt by hand. The backlog records that wording in a different shape (`could not read file: ... cannot allocate memory`). A grep of the %LOCALAPPDATA%\oshal logs finds no copy of the original output, and the 2026-09-14 WRN probe left no retained artifact either.
5. **The reason given for the stand-in is unproven.** The entry says Windows cannot make a file unreadable to the root-running scanner container. The same commit says it reproduced `permission denied` skips in the real image, so an unreadable path could be produced for the scanner somehow. Nothing in the tree shows why the gate itself could not be run that way.

Criterion 2 as originally set is therefore unmet, and the evidence shows parser logic rather than a partial scan by the real scanner failing the gate.

REFUTED: The code the triage agent cites is real and on main. 3754a367 is an ancestor of HEAD b999b05f, which equals origin/main. ci-local.sh:404 routes gate_secrets through run_secret_scan. ci-secret-scan.sh:16 and :37-52 fail on a non-zero scanner rc or on unread>0, and write `unread=N of M`. The unread-count criterion also holds on a real run: the 2026-09-14 23:30 nightly (sha 018e0a74, which contains the fix) logged `secret-scan: PASS unread=0 of 5598 exported files (scanner rc=0)` at line 3154 of %LOCALAPPDATA%\oshal\ci-local.log. The "unreadable run is shown not to pass" criterion is not met, though.

1. **The criterion was weakened by the commit that claims to meet it.** The done-when as filed in 9f482e89 (#443) said: "a run with a deliberately unreadable file in the export is shown not to pass". 3754a367 rewrote it to "a deliberately unreadable path ... (the stand-in replays the real wording ...)" and marked it "met" in the same commit.

2. **Even the rewritten wording is not literally met.** In tests/unit/ci-local-secret-scan.spec.ts, createRepo (lines 57-70) exports three readable files: .gitleaks.toml, README.md and src/app.ts. The `docker` on PATH is a stand-in script (line 103) that prints canned stderr naming /scan/config-seed/hidden.json and /scan/src/private. Neither path exists in that export. So no path in the run is unreadable and the real scanner never runs. The spec shows that the gate parses canned text correctly, not that a run over an unreadable file fails.

3. **No real scanner run has ever produced a FAIL.** The only real run of the new gate is the 09-15 PASS above. It shows the log line works; it says nothing about the unreadable case.

4. **The repo's own standard rejects a mock as closure here.** CLAUDE.md's integration-boundary corollary says a guard must not mock the built image or protocol adapter behind a defect and then claim that boundary is protected. It also says scoped doubles must be recorded with a real companion in docs/governance/real-boundary-regression-audit.md. A grep of that file for secret-scan, gitleaks and ci-local-secret finds nothing.

5. **"Fails on any unreadable path" is narrower than written.** Detection is a fixed list of five phrases (ci-secret-scan.sh:16) calibrated against gitleaks v8.30.1 (comment at line 12). Production runs `zricethezav/gitleaks:latest` (ci-local.sh:394), and the spec pins that `:latest` argument rather than a version. Nothing checks that the image actually running still writes those phrases. An unread path reported in any other wording counts as 0 and the gate passes.

6. **The reason given for using a stand-in contradicts the commit's own evidence.** The commit says Windows cannot make a file unreadable to the root-running scanner. Yet the same commit reports reproducing "permission denied" skips in the real v8.30.1 image. That reproduction was never run through gate_secrets, and no artifact of it exists on disk.

entries.title: Publish gate: refuse model-attribution trailers at push time
entries.why: This is a 'Built' record with no separate done-when. The change is merged and its 'Live when' condition holds on the shared checkout. core.hooksPath points at this checkout's .githooks, the tree is at origin/main, and the pre-push hook calls the gate with --pre-push. Check 5b refuses attributed commit messages in exactly the pushed set. PR descriptions stay out of hook reach by design; the entry itself notes that.
entries.evidence: Commit e85f9f4b 'fix(publish-gate): refuse model attribution in the commit messages a push publishes' is an ancestor of origin/main. scripts/publish-gate.sh:222-266 is section 5b, with ATTRIB_RE covering -by: trailers naming claude/anthropic, the vendor no-reply address, and 'generated with/by/using/via ... claude'. .githooks/pre-push:35 `bash "${REPO_ROOT}/scripts/publish-gate.sh" --pre-push`. `git config --get core.hooksPath` = C:\Projects\oshal\.githooks. tests/unit/publish-gate.spec.ts has a pre-push scope describe at :651 and a real-hook install at :253-265.
verifyReasons:
CONFIRMED: I couldn't refute it. I re-checked everything myself, and the entry's own conditions hold in the current tree.

The entry (BACKLOG.md:585-615) has no "Done when" line. When e85f9f4b rewrote it as a Built record, the original done-when had three criteria (visible with `git show e85f9f4b -- docs/BACKLOG.md`). I checked all three and the "Live when" condition.

1. **The gate refuses attributed commits and names them.** e85f9f4b is an ancestor of origin/main. It merged as 872981d6 (PR #455). The working tree is at b999b05f, which equals origin/main. `git ls-files --eol` shows the gate file is LF on disk and in the index, with no diff against HEAD. In `scripts/publish-gate.sh`, check 5b runs from line 222 to 266. Its pattern on line 243 catches:
   - a `-by:` trailer naming claude or anthropic
   - the vendor no-reply address anywhere
   - "generated with/by/using/via" followed by claude

   It reports each hit with the short SHA, the subject and the reword command. It judges exactly the pushed set: the ref-update lines on stdin, minus remote-tracking refs and the remote sha. A deletion is skipped, and a commit it cannot list is refused.

2. **The tests go red on an attributed commit and green on a clean one.** `tests/unit/publish-gate.spec.ts` has 13 refused rows (from :558), 4 passing rows (:578), and the range and already-published scope cases. The pre-push scope block starts at :651, and one case runs a real `git push` through the real hook (:736). The gate and the spec are unchanged since e85f9f4b (`git diff e85f9f4b HEAD` is empty for both). The hook's two later commits (6898ac59, 63324a6d) only change code after the gate call. The test skips that code with OSHAL_SKIP_PREPUSH_VERIFY=1. I could not run the tests (read-only); this rests on reading the code plus the 43/43 run recorded at commit time.

3. **The PR-description remedy is still documented.** `scripts/governance/attribution-scrub/strip_pr_footers.py` is tracked, and the runbook's step 7 (lines 108-113) documents it.

4. **"Live when" holds on the shared checkout.** `git config --show-origin` gives `file:.git/config C:\Projects\oshal\.githooks`. `.githooks/pre-push:35` runs `bash "${REPO_ROOT}/scripts/publish-gate.sh" --pre-push`, and nothing before that line reads stdin.

The live history backs this up. Using the gate's own pattern, 0 of the 63 commits on origin/main since the merge are attributed. Across all remote branches (fetched 2026-09-15 13:39), 0 of 150 commits since the merge are attributed.

Two things I checked that do not break the entry:
- **The 45 old commits.** 45 attributed commits are still reachable from origin/main. The entry explicitly leaves them out of scope and points to the runbook scrub, so they are not a done-when criterion.
- **One lane clone has no hook.** `/c/Projects/lanes/persist-retry` pushes to the GitHub origin with no core.hooksPath and only sample hooks in `.git/hooks`. It has no logged pushes. "Live when" is scoped to the shared checkout, so this is outside the entry's condition. The six other lanes set hooksPath=.githooks and carry the 5b gate.

REFUTED: The code the triage cited is real, but the "done" verdict rests on the guard's green status and on the wall being up, and neither is shown.

**What checks out (re-derived):**
- e85f9f4b is an ancestor of origin/main and of HEAD (both b999b05f).
- `scripts/publish-gate.sh:222-266` is check 5b, with ATTRIB_RE at :243. `--pre-push` reads stdin at :35-50.
- `.githooks/pre-push:35` calls the gate with `--pre-push`.
- `core.hooksPath` is `C:\Projects\oshal\.githooks`, set in `.git/config`.
- The working tree matches origin/main for the gate, the hook and the spec.
- The spec has 43 cases, 26 of them new.
- `strip_pr_footers.py` exists and is runbook step 7.
- No attributed commit landed in the 64 commits from e85f9f4b to origin/main.
- The entry has no done-when of its own. Its original one (replaced in e85f9f4b) said `tests/unit/publish-gate.spec.ts` "proves red on such a fixture commit and green on a clean one."

**Why it is refuted:**

1. **The only post-merge run of the guard is red.** `%LOCALAPPDATA%\oshal\ci-local-last-run.log:4554` is the scheduled `ci-local --head` run of 2026-09-14T23:30 against origin/main 018e0a74. That commit contains e85f9f4b, and `git diff e85f9f4b origin/main` on the spec and gate is empty, so it ran today's exact spec and gate. It reported `publish-gate.spec.ts (43 tests | 13 failed) 807704ms`. Seven of the failures are new cases from this entry:
   - names only the attributed commit in a longer range
   - does NOT re-judge history the remote already holds
   - refuses an attributed commit pushed BY SHA while HEAD is clean
   - judges only what is pushed
   - does not re-judge what the remote already has with no remote-tracking refs
   - fails closed when a pushed commit cannot be enumerated
   - the REAL git push through the REAL hook
   
   The night before, the file had 17 tests, 4 failed, and took 13.8 s (`ci-runs/ci-head-skipimage-20260913-2358.out.log:18992`). The log keeps no failure reasons. The durations (27 s to 236 s) suggest a loaded box, but the cause is not established. The "43/43 pass" in the entry comes from the builder's own run before merge. The triage cited no test result at all.

2. **The Live-when evidence covers one clone only.** It proves the wall for pushes from `C:\Projects\oshal`. `C:\Projects\lanes\persist-retry` also pushes to `emeraldcoastsystemsgroup/oshal.git` (branch fix/persistence-init-retryable). It has no `core.hooksPath` in any scope and an empty `.git/hooks`, so a push from it runs no publish gate at all. The hook's own Change Log (SEQ 8, `.githooks/pre-push:14`) says shared clones are "how parallel agents work here now." The other lanes use a relative `.githooks`, so each runs its own tree's hook.

Until the spec is shown green on main, this entry is not demonstrably done.

entries.title: The Windows purge abandon can say it could not enumerate, but still cannot enumerate
entries.why: Windows still has no process-table reader. purge_tree_process_table still shells out to `ps -eo pid=,ppid=`, which Git Bash refuses, so the abandon still falls through to UNCHECKED when taskkill /T is absent or refused. Closing it means one reader (bare `ps` PID/PPID/WINPID, or tasklist keyed by WINPID), a deepest-first kill by Windows pid, and a spec case with a real native grandchild. The spec's current win32 assertion also has to change from refusal to a usable table.

No WINPID or tasklist reader exists in the file; the only Windows-pid use is purge_tree_winpid feeding taskkill at :52-57 and :127-134. tests/unit/ci-local-purge.spec.ts:330-335 pins win32 to `table_rc=2` / `walk_rc=2` / `list=[]`, so refusal is the asserted contract today. entries.title: Gemini one-click harness login
entries.why: This entry asks for an ECSG Google OAuth client and start/callback/signout routes so a Gemini-harness bot can run on the result. Three later decisions in the tree rule that out: Gemini login stays status-only and runs through the vendor's own login, a Google sign-in does not grant Gemini access, and unattended gemini-cli execution fails closed. With the harness refused, the done-when ('a Gemini-harness bot answers') cannot be reached.
entries.evidence: src/app/routes/gemini-auth-routes.ts:6 change log: 'Status-ONLY by operator doctrine: the vendor's own CLI login runs host-side (Connect-AI.bat / run `gemini` once) — no /start, no /callback, no Google OAuth client here, ever' (the file has only GET /status). src/features/llm-provider/services/unattended-provider-policy.ts:14 puts 'gemini-cli' in UNBROKERED_AUTONOMOUS_PROVIDERS, which assertAuditedAutonomousHarness refuses. The same refusal is in any-bot/server/services/llm/assert-cli-tool-boundary.js ('gemini', 'gemini-cli'). CLAUDE.md:224 says gemini-cli has 'Unattended execution disabled; local OAuth presence is diagnostic only'. docs/adr/090-skills-as-first-class-packages.md:276 says OAuth homes are 'populated by the vendor's own login flow (never brokered — ToS)'. docs/adr/064-free-tier-llm-access.md:175 says Sign in with Google does not grant Gemini; treat it as paste-a-key. docs/backlog/archive/2026-08-05-partial-item-history.md:587 rates the one-click Gemini request 'Half wrong'.
verifyReasons:
REFUTED: The entry is not done, and the evidence doesn't show it was superseded.

1. No done-when criterion is met. src/app/routes/gemini-auth-routes.ts has only GET /status. Nothing in src or any-bot/server implements a Gemini /start, /callback or /signout route. There is no ECSG Google OAuth client and no Google consent flow, so no Gemini-harness bot has answered on minted credentials.

2. The "later decisions" are not later. git log shows two groups:
- Some are already in the 2026-07-23 cutover snapshot 41d4784a: the status-only doctrine in gemini-auth-routes.ts, the matching server.ts comments (changelog entry 103 and the lines 1199-1201 mount comment: "we never broker Google OAuth"), ADR-064:175 and ADR-090's "never brokered" line.
- The rest were created in commit 76d5788e on 2026-08-06: unattended-provider-policy.ts, assert-cli-tool-boundary.js, CLAUDE.md:224's "Unattended execution disabled" row and the 2026-08-05 archive with the "Half wrong" verdict.

76d5788e is the same commit that wrote this entry into the active queue. Its sub-commits are "docs(backlog): restore active-only queue" and "docs(backlog): archive resolved provider boundary". The author archived the resolved provider items and kept this one active, with every cited decision already in the tree. Before that, the entry was the "Plan E" item marked "Verified 2026-07-19: PARTIAL ... the Gemini OAuth popup-redirect route is still unbuilt".

3. The harness refusal is conditional, not permanent. unattended-provider-policy.ts says these providers "may be restored only behind a separately audited brokered sandbox". CLAUDE.md says the same. So the done-when is blocked by a missing prerequisite, not impossible. codex-cli is in the same refused set, yet openai-codex-oauth-routes.ts still has /start, /callback, /status and /signout, hardened during the SEC-05 closure. A refused harness has not made its login flow obsolete.

4. ADR-064:175 covers a different path. It says a Google sign-in doesn't grant the AI Studio free-tier key. The entry leaves that path out on purpose ("AI Studio key paste remains a separate existing path"). It targets Gemini Code Assist credentials, the ~/.gemini/oauth_creds.json that the gemini CLI's own login writes. The snapshot's Plan E text calls that option "the only true popup-redirect path". The archive's "Half wrong" verdict was about parity with Anthropic, not a rejection of the Gemini OAuth work.

5. It is still tracked elsewhere. docs/backlog/non-human-checklist.md:119 lists "[H] OAuth app reviews: Gemini one-click login" as an open human-only item.

The status-only comment in gemini-auth-routes.ts ("no Google OAuth client here, ever") does conflict with the entry. But it is an older code comment, and the backlog entry was curated after it. Settling that conflict is the operator's call; it doesn't show the entry is stale.

REFUTED: The entry is not done, and the evidence does not show it was superseded. The triage says three "later decisions" rule it out, but none of them came after the entry.

1. **Done-when is not met.** The file src/app/routes/gemini-auth-routes.ts has only GET /status. There is no start, callback or signout route. `GeminiCliHarnessAdapter.run` (gemini-cli-harness-adapter.ts:138) and `HarnessLLMBridge.sendRequest` (harness-adapter.ts:167) both call `assertAuditedAutonomousHarness`, and that refusal is unconditional. The ADR-127 DEMO_MODE exception covers only Claude Code and Codex (any-bot assert-cli-tool-boundary.js; docs/guides/cloud-and-connections.md:67-69), so it does not help Gemini.

2. **The dates do not support "later".** The entry was created in commit 76d5788e (2026-08-06). That same commit also wrote:
   - the CLAUDE.md:224 row saying gemini-cli fails closed,
   - the whole unattended-provider-policy.ts file,
   - the archive's "Half wrong" verdict.

   The ADR-064 and ADR-090 lines date back to the initial import commit (41d4784a), before this entry existed. The status-only route with its "no Google OAuth client here, ever" note is from 2026-07-19 (private archive commit c7062dcc). So whoever restored the backlog added this item on 2026-08-06 with all of this already in the tree. It restates Plan E option (a) from the original backlog (41d4784a:1566-1586). No later commit touches the item. The only later changes to the refusal policy are the ADR-127 exceptions, which relaxed it rather than tightening it.

3. **Blocked is not the same as superseded.** gemini-cli is still in `HarnessType` and in `HARNESS_FACTORIES` (provider-runtime.ts:106 and :249). The policy says these providers "may be restored only behind a separately audited brokered sandbox". CLAUDE.md likewise says to re-enable them only after an audited brokered sandbox exists. The done-when is waiting on that, not impossible.

4. **ADR-064:175 is about a different credential.** It covers the identity-only Google sign-in (`openid email profile`) and the AI Studio free-tier key. This entry is about Gemini Code Assist credentials and says AI Studio key paste "remains a separate existing path". The original Plan E notes that `gemini auth login` uses Google OAuth with Code Assist scopes.

5. **"Half wrong" rejects a different claim.** The wrong half is the idea that Anthropic already had one-click login. The verdict does not reject Gemini login.

6. **The tree has no rule against in-browser vendor logins.** claude-code-auth-routes.ts has /start, /callback, /submit-code and /signout. openai-codex-oauth-routes.ts has /start, /callback, /status and /signout. Gemini is the only one missing, and that gap is what this entry tracks. The ADR-090 line about the vendor's own login flow ("never brokered — ToS") is the strongest point for the triage. Even so, it is about per-user OAuth home directories and predates the entry.

7. **Other docs still list it as open.** docs/backlog/non-human-checklist.md:119 lists "[H] OAuth app reviews: Gemini one-click login" as a human-gated item.

At most, the "no Google OAuth client here, ever" change-log note conflicts with a backlog entry that was added later. That conflict is for the operator to decide, not evidence that the entry is stale.

entries.title: Complete and cancel nightly backup checks safely
entries.why: The trunk's backup diagnostic still has the exact defect that was observed. psql runs with ON_ERROR_STOP=0 inside `sh -c` without pipefail, so a cancelled or failed pg_dump still exits 0. Only the `agents` row count is compared, so a partial restore can pass. There is no statement/lock timeout and no check of the deploy lock. The fix is hardening this script (strict exit codes, full-restore verification, bounded run and cleanup, deploy-lock coordination) plus regressions registered in the AI Test Lab. Those regressions must hit a real Postgres to prove the lock behaviour. The scheduled-launcher leg overlaps BACKLOG 'Nightly tasks still launched from the ADR-115 archive'.

entries.why: The connector list now sends a credential-free `expired` boolean on every connection, and Identity Hub reads it for the Reconnect pill, the '· expired' marker, the Need-attention tile count and the needs-attention filter. Both sides of the contract are pinned by unit guards. The shipped rule is 'lapsed and unrenewable' rather than a bare `expiry < now`. That was deliberate: 9 of 24 live connections had a past expiry but carried refresh tokens, so the naive rule would have flagged healthy accounts. BUG-13's resolution records this. A lapsed grant that can't be renewed does render as expired.
entries.evidence: Core 867b43d9 'fix(connectors): tell the Identity Hub which logins are actually broken (BUG-13) (#193)', 2026-08-12. `src/app/routes/connector-response-helpers.ts:90` has `expired: isConnectionExpired(connection)`, and `src/app/routes/connector-tenancy.ts:203` defines `isConnectionExpired`. `tests/unit/connector-list-expiry.spec.ts` pins CONNECTION_KEYS including 'expired' on both provider and any-llm entries, checks the flag end to end (a lapsed connection with no refresh token gives true), and checks that no token material appears. Store c717010 (#68): `identity/tests/identity-list-contract.test.js` asserts the surface reads only promised keys and reads `c.expired` at least 4 times. `identity/tools/identity.html:606-610` covers the pill and marker, `:631-642` feeds countExpired into the 'Need attention' tile, and `:650-652` is the filter. `docs/operations/bug-log.md` BUG-13 has 'Resolution (2026-08-12)'.
verifyReasons:
REFUTED: The code the triage agent cites is real. Two of the entry's done-when criteria are still not met as written.

What checks out:
- Commit 867b43d9 (#193) is an ancestor of main.
- `connector-response-helpers.ts:90` emits `expired: isConnectionExpired(connection)`, and `byo-llm-routes.ts` carries the same key on the any-llm entry.
- `/list` reads through `accessibleConnections`, whose `CONN_COLS` include `expiry` and `refresh_token`.
- `tests/unit/connector-list-expiry.spec.ts` is in the vitest include set (`tests/unit/**/*.spec.ts`).
- In the store, c717010 is on HEAD. `identity.html` reads `c.expired` at :606, :610, :632 and :650, and `identity-list-contract.test.js` is registered in `identity/tests/test-lab.yaml`.

Criterion 1 is not met. It says "a connection whose stored token has passed its expiry renders the expired marker and is counted by the Need-attention tile and filter." The shipped rule (`connector-tenancy.ts:203-210`) returns false whenever `refresh_token` is present, however far past expiry the row is.
- The fix commit and BUG-13's Resolution both say 9 live connections had a past expiry and the tile "reads 0 on this deployment". So for every live connection that fits the criterion's wording, the marker does not render.
- The team changed the meaning of "expired" on purpose, but never amended the entry's done-when. That text still asks for the old behaviour, and it still says the response "never emits" the flag, which is now out of date.

The new meaning also misses the actually broken case, not just healthy renewing logins:
- `getValidAccessToken` (`connector-account-operations.ts:181`) throws `refresh 4xx` when the provider rejects a grant. It does not clear `refresh_token` or update `expiry`.
- Its own doc comment and `connector-liveness.ts` record this happening: a revoked Testing-mode Google grant on the G-Squared box.
- Such a row keeps a lapsed expiry and a dead refresh token, so `isConnectionExpired` returns false for it indefinitely.
- Identity Hub reads only `/api/connect/list`. Grepping for liveness or `needs_reconnect` in `identity.html` and `identity-routes.ts` finds nothing.
- Result: a login that has actually expired and cannot renew never shows "· expired" and is never counted in Need attention.
- The core Connections screen handles this case: `src/api/utilities.html:385` sets `dead = c.expired || live.status==='needs_reconnect'`. That shows the codebase knows `expired` alone misses these grants.

Criterion 2 is only partly met. The unit assertion pins the six per-connection keys. It does not pin the provider-level keys Identity Hub reads.
- `p.configured` drives the needs-attention filter (`identity.html:652`) and the Ready-to-enable tile.
- No unit spec asserts `configured` in the `buildConnectorListResponse` output. `connectors-routes-decomposition.spec.ts` omits it, and only the Playwright e2e specs for Plaid and SmartThings check it.
- The store test scrapes only `c.<key>` reads.
- So a projection that dropped `configured` would not fail any unit assertion.

REFUTED: Refuted. The plumbing the triage agent describes is real, but neither done-when criterion is fully met as written.

What checks out: 867b43d9 is an ancestor of HEAD (b999b05f). `connector-response-helpers.ts` projects `expired: isConnectionExpired(connection)`, and the any-llm entry in `byo-llm-routes.ts` does the same. `/api/connect/list` returns `{providers: buildConnectorListResponse(rows)}`, and `accessibleConnections` selects `refresh_token` and `expiry`. In the store, c717010 is on origin/main, and `identity/tools/identity.html` reads `c.expired` at :606 (pill), :610 (marker), :631-642 (countExpired feeding the "Need attention" tile) and :650-652 (filter).

Criterion 1: "a connection whose stored token has passed its expiry renders the expired marker and is counted by the Need-attention tile and filter". This is NOT met.
- `connector-tenancy.ts:203-209` returns false whenever `refresh_token` is present. So a connection whose stored token has passed its expiry but still holds a refresh token never shows the marker. That was a deliberate redefinition, recorded in BUG-13's Resolution. But the BACKLOG done-when was never amended. `git log -L` shows the entry has not changed since 100ca097, and it still says the flag is "never emitted".
- The redefinition also misses a real broken-login case. When a provider revokes a grant (for example a Testing-mode Google refresh token that returns `refresh 400`), `getValidAccessToken` (`connector-account-operations.ts`) throws and leaves the row untouched: `refresh_token` stays set and `expiry` stays in the past. `isConnectionExpired` therefore returns false. The only thing that detects this case is the separate `/api/connect/liveness` probe (`connector-liveness.ts`, `needs_reconnect`), and Identity Hub never reads it. A grep of `identity/` finds no liveness or `needs_reconnect` usage. So the claim that "a lapsed grant that can't be renewed does render as expired" holds only for grants that never had a refresh token.
- No test renders the surface. The store guard only counts `c.expired` regex matches (at least 4). It cannot show that the marker, tile or filter actually render.

Criterion 2: "a unit assertion pins the response keys the shipped surfaces read, so dropping a consumed field goes red". This is only partly met.
- `tests/unit/connector-list-expiry.spec.ts` pins only the per-connection keys (CONNECTION_KEYS).
- The store guard only checks `c.<key>` reads.
- The Identity Hub surface also reads `p.tokenFallback` in `isTokenSetup` (identity.html:569), which feeds the "Ready to enable" tile (:638) and the action buttons (:579). No test in either repo pins it: grep finds `tokenFallback` in no core test and no `identity/tests` file. Dropping it from `buildConnectorListResponse` would not go red.
- `configured` is pinned only incidentally, by the Plaid Playwright spec, not by a unit assertion. The decomposition spec's `toMatchObject` covers neither `configured` nor `tokenFallback`.

entries.title: Finance workspace navigation
entries.why: The done-when is met and natively accepted. Admitted Finance is a curated top workspace (/cockpit/?app=finance), Home has a named Finance area with grouped updates and no Other shelf, and the OSHAL menu keeps Home, the searchable All applications list and the remaining workspaces. Only the explicitly delegated Finance sidebar entry is removed, and unrelated financial tools and per-app permissions are preserved. Both commits are on main, and the release record captures native Chrome acceptance on the deployed image.
entries.evidence: Commits 0c287223 ('feat(cockpit): compose daily Jarvis dashboard and Finance navigation') and d8080f56 (modal centering) are both ancestors of origin/main (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`). src/pages/cockpit/js/workspace-navigation.js:20 CURATED includes ['finance']; config-seed/profiles/oshal-framework.json:440 has "workspace": "finance"; src/pages/cockpit/js/views/app-home-daily.js:11 maps 'ai-finance' to 'Finance'. Tests: tests/unit/workspace-navigation-model.spec.ts:76-82 (only Finance is delegated; payroll, ai-finance suite and the Money group are not), tests/unit/app-home-browser.spec.ts:81,101-134 (Finance area present, absent and unavailable), npm scripts test:workspace-navigation and test:daily-dashboard (package.json:50-51). docs/releases/daily-dashboard-2026-09-13.md 'Installed acceptance': native Chrome verified the named Finance area and top workspace, OSHAL menu placement, and Finance opening /cockpit/?app=finance with its sidebar, on image e92d3468 with 35/35 healthy. docs/backlog/cockpit-workspace-navigation.md:152-160 marks it 'Delivered presentation'.
verifyReasons:
CONFIRMED: I could not refute it. I re-checked every done-when item in the current tree (HEAD b999b05f = origin/main), and each one holds up.

1. **Both commits are on main.** 0c287223 and d8080f56 are ancestors of both origin/main and HEAD. Later commits that touch these files are aba0e31f (RibbonNav locked tiles, which still passes `workspace` through and spreads `...tile`), the discovery-route cancellation change, and 5e1348ba (maker-lab tiles). None of them regresses the Finance delegation, CURATED, dailyAreas or the menu.

2. **Finance is a named top workspace.**
   - workspace-navigation.js:20 has CURATED = little-monsters, create, intelligent-career/career-hunter, capture-crm, finance.
   - The server route workspace-navigation-routes.ts admits a destination only if it is active, discoverable, not access-denied, and its initial surface passes canNavigateHttpPath.
   - The Finance manifest in the store has `theme: graphite` and `defaultView: finance-home` with `iframeUrl /api/finance/`, so it qualifies for discovery.
   - Below 640 px, a compact disclosure opens the workspace links. Between that and full width, the links scroll horizontally and scroll into view when focused.

3. **The OSHAL menu.** It is a `<details>` beside the brand containing Home, an All applications button, search and the utilities. It is anchored with positionMore, and Escape returns focus to the trigger. All applications opens the full home-plan directory through bindApplicationsDirectory, which is wired in app.js:177. From a focused app it goes to /cockpit/?view=home&directory=1.

4. **No `Other` shelf on Home.** app-home-daily.js dailyAreas keeps only the seven known suite labels, with ai-finance shown as "Finance". sectionBySuite keeps `Other` for the internal catalog only. Failed probes show as "Updates unavailable", never as zero. The Jarvis page groups tasks by source with counts (jarvis-dashboard.js).

5. **Delegation is explicit only.** The only new delegation is `"workspace": "finance"` on tool-finance-home (oshal-framework.json:440). Payroll, Intelligent Trades and Kalshi (the Money group) keep their tiles. isWorkspaceDelegated needs exact metadata on the oshal-framework profile, and the model spec (lines 76-82) proves that payroll, the ai-finance suite, the Money group and the Finance label do not delegate.

6. **Test coverage and Test Lab registration.**
   - The contextual browser spec covers Finance appearing, unrelated tools like payroll being kept, and Finance being revoked with the draft kept.
   - The Home browser spec covers the Finance area shown, hidden (absent) and unavailable, plus directory access, 390 px width, 200% zoom and three themes.
   - None of these specs contains a skip.
   - Both suites are in `npm run test:workspace-navigation` and `test:daily-dashboard`, and are registered in Test Lab as cockpit-workspace-navigation and cockpit-daily-dashboard (wired in test-lab-scenarios.ts:235-236).

7. **Installed acceptance.** The native Chrome receipts in temp/ exist and their SHA256 values match the release record (296144e2…, cb286bfb…). They list Finance as a daily area and top workspace, and Finance opening /cockpit/?app=finance on image e92d3468.

The work still open is durable grouping, snooze and replay (JDX-03), more report producers (JDX-04), context actions (JDX-05) and the startup-delay investigation. Each of those is tracked in its own entry, and this entry's text scopes itself to presentation only.

REFUTED: Most of the claim holds up. What I confirmed in the current tree:
- 0c287223 and d8080f56 are both ancestors of origin/main, and nothing later reverts them.
- workspace-navigation.js:20 has finance in CURATED.
- oshal-framework.json:440 marks only tool-finance-home as `workspace: finance`. Intelligent Trades and Kalshi stay in the Money group.
- app-home-daily.js:24 drops the `other` shelf from the daily areas.
- The OSHAL menu offers Home, All applications, search and the settings controls.
- Both native acceptance receipts exist in temp/ and their SHA256 values match the release record.

The entry is still not fully done. Its done-when says the daily dashboard must "show authorized Finance destinations", and that is only true for the top tabs.

1. **Home does not check authorization.** Home's Finance area and the All applications list both come from GET /api/swarm/apps/home-plan (swarm-app-routes.ts:272-281). That route filters only by install scope: listApps, then isVisibleToCaller in swarm-app-record-view.ts:108. It never calls the application-authorization canDiscover check or the appAccess deny tier. The top tabs do check: /api/ui/workspaces calls canDiscover at workspace-navigation-routes.ts:47 and the deny tier at line 48.

2. **Under the default mode this shows Finance to people without access.** The default authorization mode is `enforce` (application-authorization-runtime.ts:45-46), and in that mode packages are protected (line 100). The finance manifest (oshal-applications finance/oshal-app.yaml) declares no `scope:`, so it installs as public and every signed-in user can see it. A user with no Finance role therefore:
   - does not get the Finance top tab, but
   - still sees Finance in Home's Finance area, with its update checks failing as "Updates unavailable", and
   - still sees Finance with an Open button in the All applications list.

   When a Finance role is revoked, the top tab disappears but the Home entries stay.

3. **The tests don't cover this for Home.** The navigation follow-up requires the browser and authorization suites to cover "Finance present/absent/revoked". The Home browser test "retracts a no-longer-admitted entry" (app-home-browser.spec.ts:174) runs against a fake home-plan fixture that simply drops the entry, which the real route does not do on revocation. The only real authorization-route suite (workspace-navigation-routes.spec.ts) has no Finance or Home case. So the "authorized" and "revoked" behaviour of the daily dashboard is not tested against the real server.

A smaller gap: the top-row checks at narrow widths (768 and 390 px) run on a fixture with only four workspaces, and none of them is Finance. The only test with Finance in the top row runs at 1440 px. So the requirement that named workspaces stay reachable at narrow widths is not tested with Finance present.

entries.title: Lazy-DDL trigger and function guards must converge, not create-once
entries.why: The real-boundary case ran green in a ci-local.sh --head run on an origin/main SHA that includes the change that added it. All 9 tests in the spec file passed, none skipped or failed, and that includes 'renders every known by-name guard on a real Postgres exactly as its pinned live definition'. That is the entry's done-when.
entries.evidence: %LOCALAPPDATA%/oshal/ci-local.log:3125 shows the run 'LOCAL CI start (scheduled=1 head=1 ...) sha=018e0a74cf09'. %LOCALAPPDATA%/oshal/ci-local-last-run.log:16042 shows '✓ tests/unit/person-model-parity-postgres.spec.ts (9 tests) 37729ms' at 2026-09-15 00:36. `git show 018e0a74:tests/unit/person-model-parity-postgres.spec.ts` has 9 it() blocks, and the guard case is at :152. 923b69e6 (#467, which added the case) is an ancestor of 018e0a74. tests/helpers/lazy-ddl-guards.ts and person-model-schema.ts are unchanged between 018e0a74 and HEAD. The spec changed since then only in its DSN resolver (fcd68539). Keeping it green: that run connected through the old 127.0.0.1:55433 fallback. Since fcd68539 the spec throws unless PERSON_MODEL_TEST_DSN or TEST_DATABASE_URL is set (tests/helpers/spec-database-url.ts), and scripts/ci-local.sh:262 gate_unit sets neither.
verifyReasons:
REFUTED: The historical run did happen, but the done-when is not met in the current tree.

The run checks out:
- ci-local.log:3125 shows the scheduled run with head=1 at sha=018e0a74cf09.
- ci-local-last-run.log:16042 shows "✓ tests/unit/person-model-parity-postgres.spec.ts (9 tests)". This is vitest 4.1.9, which would have printed a skipped or failed count if there was one.
- 923b69e6 is an ancestor of 018e0a74, and the guard case is at :152.
- Between 018e0a74 and HEAD, lazy-ddl-guards.ts and src/features/person-model are unchanged.

It does not hold in the current tree:
- fcd68539 (committed 2026-09-15 01:23, after that CI run ended at 01:12) changed the spec's DSN to `specDatabaseUrl(['PERSON_MODEL_TEST_DSN','TEST_DATABASE_URL'])`.
- In tests/helpers/spec-database-url.ts, that resolver has no default. It throws when neither variable is set. It also throws when the DSN lands on 127.0.0.1:55433, unless OSHAL_ALLOW_LIVE_STACK_DB=1, which nothing in the repo sets.
- scripts/ci-local.sh:262 (gate_unit) sets neither variable, and vitest.config.ts loads no env.
- `git grep` at HEAD finds nothing that sets either variable. scripts/ci/run-nightly-isolated.mjs actually blanks TEST_DATABASE_URL.
- So `ci-local.sh --head` on today's tree would fail the whole file at module load, the guard case included. It would not be green.
- fcd68539's own commit message and the BACKLOG entry it added ("The DB-backed unit specs need a disposable PostgreSQL…") say these 23 specs "now REFUSE rather than run" and "the local-CI unit gate cannot execute them".

The one green run is also weak evidence:
- It connected through the old 127.0.0.1:55433 fallback. The repo now calls that the operator's live trading Postgres and refuses it.
- The companion entry "Real-Postgres specs cannot run from this host while Docker port publishing is wedged" is still open.

In short, the case passed once on a tree and connection path that are now gone, and on the current tree it cannot run green. The criterion is unmet, so the entry is not done.

REFUTED: The triage agent's historical facts check out. The guard case is not green from `ci-local.sh --head` in the current tree, though, and the next run would be red.

What checks out:
- `ci-local.log` shows the scheduled `--head` run at sha=018e0a74cf09.
- `ci-local-last-run.log:16042` shows `person-model-parity-postgres.spec.ts (9 tests)` passing with no skipped count.
- At 018e0a74 the spec has 9 it() blocks, and the guard case is at :152.
- `KNOWN_BY_NAME_GUARDS` held 2 entries at that SHA, so the case did not pass on an empty list.
- 923b69e6 is an ancestor of 018e0a74.

That is one historical pass. The done-when ("that case is green from ci-local.sh --head once the engine is repaired") is not met at HEAD (b999b05f):

1. **The spec no longer defaults to any database.** fcd68539 is an ancestor of HEAD (committed 2026-09-15 01:23, after the 00:36 run). It changed the spec to `const ADMIN_DSN = specDatabaseUrl(['PERSON_MODEL_TEST_DSN','TEST_DATABASE_URL'])`. `tests/helpers/spec-database-url.ts` throws when neither variable is set. Because the call is at module top level, the whole file fails to load, guard case included.

2. **Nothing supplies those variables in CI.**
   - `scripts/ci-local.sh:262` gate_unit runs `npm run test:unit` and sets neither.
   - `grep` over `scripts/ci-local.sh` and `scripts/ci/*.sh` finds no TEST_DATABASE_URL, PERSON_MODEL_TEST_DSN or OSHAL_ALLOW_LIVE_STACK_DB. The only `DATABASE_URL` is for the e2e gate on port 25432.
   - `vitest.config.ts` has no global setup that sets them.
   - The shell environment and the Windows User and Machine environment variables are all empty for all three.

3. **The one green run went through a path the repo now refuses.** That run used the old fallback `127.0.0.1:${OSHAL_PG_PORT ?? '55433'}`. Port 55433 is the live stack's published Postgres (`ci-local.sh:117`, `host-database-url.ts:15` `DEFAULT_PUBLISHED_PG_PORT='55433'`). The resolver now refuses that host and port even when set explicitly, unless `OSHAL_ALLOW_LIVE_STACK_DB=1`, and fcd68539 describes it as the operator's real trading database. So the pass cannot be repeated through a sanctioned path.

4. **No `--head` run has happened since fcd68539.** `ci-local.log` ends at 2026-09-15T01:12:44, and the last "LOCAL CI start" is the 018e0a74 run. Nothing shows the case green in the current tree; the tree shows the next `ci-local.sh --head` would fail this file at module load.

The triage agent's own evidence admits the spec now throws in `ci-local.sh`. That makes the done-when criterion unmet for the current tree, so the entry should stay open. It needs a disposable Postgres DSN wired into gate_unit, or an in-container run, then a fresh green `--head` run.

entries.title: `jarvis-routes.ts` is over the decomposition threshold
entries.why: PR #466 met the done-when. jarvis-routes.ts is at 732 code lines, the recall hook was not touched, and the jarvis specs covering the moved code passed on the committed tree. The BACKLOG still reads 'Remaining: 802 code lines' only because a later docs commit reverted the Done text.
entries.evidence: `npx eslint src/app/routes/jarvis-routes.ts` with the rule max-lines {max:1, skipComments, skipBlankLines} reports 'File has too many lines (732)'. The last commit touching the file is df652727 (#466), which moved the thread-ticket code to src/app/routes/jarvis-thread-tickets.ts. That commit's diff changes no recall-hook lines (only change-log line 51). The hook sits at jarvis-routes.ts:649 and :722 and is pinned by tests/unit/person-model-surface.spec.ts:51-53. The PR #466 body lists as green: jarvis-surface-context, jarvis-task-lifecycle, person-model-surface, jarvis-speaker-wiring and 6 other specs. The 6 failures it reports in jarvis-artifact-routing, jarvis-provider-intent-routing, jarvis-catalog-block and machine-write-identity reproduced on untouched origin/main 5e1348ba. df652727 wrote 'Done (2026-09-14)' into this entry; fea4f721 (#471) then restored the old Remaining text (`git log -S 'reads 732 (was 804'`).
verifyReasons:
REFUTED: The entry has three done-when criteria. Two are met and one is not, so it is not done.

Met:
1. **Under 800 code lines.** An AST count (TypeScript parser, comments and blank lines excluded) of src/app/routes/jarvis-routes.ts at HEAD b999b05f gives 732. The grep method gives the same. jarvis-thread-tickets.ts is 92.
2. **Recall hook unchanged.** The hook region (df652727^ lines 735-830 against HEAD lines 641-736: detectPersonModelIntent, ownerHasAmbientData, answerPersonModelIntent, the 'ambient recall failed' path) is byte-identical before and after #466.

Not met:
3. **"The existing jarvis specs green."** At least one jarvis spec is red on the current tree, and it fails against jarvis-routes.ts itself. In tests/unit/jarvis-catalog-block.spec.ts:88-92, the regex `/const ctxBlocks = \[([^\]]*)\]/` stops at the first `]` in jarvis-routes.ts:696, which reads `[tools, catalog, openWork, artifactBlock, ...(artifactSelection ? [] : [PLAN_DIRECTIVE_GUIDANCE])]`. The match ends at `...(artifactSelection ? [`. The index of 'PLAN_DIRECTIVE_GUIDANCE' is then -1, so `expect(order.indexOf('catalog') /*7*/).toBeLessThan(-1)` fails. I evaluated the regex against the file with node. Neither the spec nor that line has changed since (the line came in with 62e9e4c1).

PR #466's own body says the same. It lists failures in jarvis-catalog-block, jarvis-artifact-routing and jarvis-provider-intent-routing, and the last two drive createJarvisRoutes directly. Its argument that these failures came before the PR explains why they exist. It does not meet a criterion that asks for the jarvis specs to be green. The "reproduced on origin/main 5e1348ba" claim is only asserted in the PR body. No later commit touched those spec files, and no BACKLOG entry tracks them, so closing this entry would lose the only record that the router's specs are not green.

The PR also ran only 10 named specs. Several other specs that import or read jarvis-routes, or are jarvis specs, are not reported as run: jarvis-dashboard-assets, route-schema-validate-only, visual-response, swarm-cli, jarvis-schedule-intent, jarvis-tool-catalog and jarvis-attachments.

The triage agent narrowed the criterion to "the jarvis specs covering the moved code". The entry's done-when does not say that.

REFUTED: Two of the three done-when criteria check out. The third, "with the existing jarvis specs green", does not. The evidence the triage agent quotes shows it failing.

Criteria that hold (re-derived):
1. **Below 800 code lines.** A TypeScript AST count that skips comments and blank lines gives 732 for src/app/routes/jarvis-routes.ts at HEAD b999b05f (same as origin/main). The same method gives 804 at df652727^ and 92 for jarvis-thread-tickets.ts. No commit after df652727 touches the router.
3. **Recall hook unchanged.** The only recall-related line in df652727's diff is change-log SEQ 17. The recallIntent / doRecall / answerPersonModelIntent / ownerHasAmbientData lines are identical before and after the commit.

Criterion that is not met:
2. **Jarvis specs green.** PR #466's own commit body and its BACKLOG Done text report failures in jarvis-artifact-routing (1), jarvis-provider-intent-routing (1) and jarvis-catalog-block (1). These are not unrelated specs:
   - jarvis-artifact-routing.spec.ts:28/167 and jarvis-provider-intent-routing.spec.ts:31-35/262 mount createJarvisRoutes.
   - jarvis-catalog-block.spec.ts:88 reads jarvis-routes.ts source directly.

   They are exactly the specs this criterion is about. The done-when has no exception for failures that were already there. "They predate the change" argues about cause, and it cannot be checked read-only. It was also measured on 5e1348ba, not on the PR's actual parent d7519767 (three commits apart, one touching src/app/routes).

   Since df652727, `git log df652727..HEAD` shows no commit touching those three specs or their subject modules. `grep` of BACKLOG.md finds no entry tracking the reds. So no evidence exists that they are green in the current tree.

   The triage agent narrowed the criterion to "the jarvis specs covering the moved code". The entry does not say that. The PR also reported nothing for other specs that drive the same router: jarvis-dashboard-assets.spec.ts:11, the jarvis-briefing-* specs via tests/fixtures/jarvis-briefings.ts:17, visual-response.spec.ts:19 and route-schema-validate-only.spec.ts:10.

It is true that fea4f721 (#471, a trading-backlog docs commit) put back the older "Remaining: 802" text. That does not make the entry done, because criterion 2 was never met.
